name: Textual Backdoor Learning Benchmark
description: Textual backdoor attacks are a kind of practical threat to NLP systems. By injecting a backdoor in the training phase, the adversary could control model predictions via predefined triggers. As various attack and defense models have been proposed, it is of great significance to perform rigorous evaluations. However, we highlight two issues in previous backdoor learning evaluations: (1) The differences between real-world scenarios (e.g. releasing poisoned datasets or models) are neglected, and we argue that each scenario has its own constraints and concerns, thus requires specific evaluation protocols; (2) The evaluation metrics only consider whether the attacks could flip the models' predictions on poisoned samples and retain performances on benign samples, but ignore that poisoned samples should also be stealthy and semantic-preserving. general_score_metric: attack success rate / clean accuracy / stealthiness composite
typical_sota_score: 80–100% (attack success rate for strong textual backdoor attacks; defenses aim to drive this much lower)
reputation: A specialized research benchmark used in the NLP security community for evaluating textual backdoor attacks and defenses under realistic threat models.
notes: Non-LLM security benchmark; results depend on attack scenario and often trade off attack success, clean accuracy, and trigger stealthiness.
